title: Member of Technical Staff (Site Reliability Engineer, Crawler)
description:
Keeping a crawler running is not the same as keeping it productive. Queues can grow while servers look healthy, and a small change can become a fleet-wide bottleneck. On Perplexity's Crawler team, you'll improve throughput, plan capacity, and build operational reliability through safer deployments, better observability, and durable fixes.



Responsibilities

 - Operate and optimize Kubernetes workloads and supporting infrastructure for crawler services, including fetching and rendering fleets.

 - Build and maintain infrastructure as code and CI/CD pipelines, with safe rollouts, validation, and fast rollback.

 - Define SLOs and build monitoring, alerting, and observability for availability, latency, throughput, and resource saturation.

 - Own capacity planning and resource efficiency; diagnose queue backlogs, network failures, and resource bottlenecks with service owners.

 - Participate in the team's on-call rotation, lead incident response, and turn blameless postmortems into durable reliability improvements.

 - Write production software to automate diagnosis and routine remediation, with validation and approval gates for high-impact actions.



Qualifications

 - 5+ years of experience in SRE, production engineering, or infrastructure-heavy backend roles, with strong programming skills in Python, C++, Rust, or Go.

 - Hands-on experience with cloud infrastructure, production Kubernetes, infrastructure as code such as Terraform, and automated deployment workflows.

 - Strong Linux and networking fundamentals, including TCP/IP, DNS, TLS, HTTP, and load balancing.

 - Experience building observability with tools such as Datadog, Prometheus, or Grafana, and using SLOs to guide reliability improvements.

 - Proven experience diagnosing distributed-system failures, leading production incidents, and improving system performance or resource efficiency.



Nice to have

 - Experience operating web crawlers, search infrastructure, or browser fleets at scale.

 - Experience with distributed queues, backpressure, workload isolation, or multi-region recovery.
